chapter: San Francisco and the postwar slump
title: Western Avenue: the Ringside and Hi-De-Ho Club
summary: With Central Avenue clubs closing, Western Avenue took over, including Alton Redd's Ringside and the Hi-De-Ho Club.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Most of the clubs on Central Avenue and the east side had folded, and things were beginning to move west music-wise. The next big music stop was Western Avenue. And it had places like the Ringside on Washington and Western. I used to play over there with Vi Redd's father, Alton Redd. He used to hire Wardell and me over there to play with them

quite often, and then just other guys would come in to jam. And the Hi-De-Ho Club. That's where Charlie Parker worked down with Wardell Gray, and Hampton, and Howard McGhee had the band. That's where they were when they recorded "Relaxin' At Camarillo," the recording...
Might have been. Might have been. Yeah, that was at 50th and Western, a club called the Hi-De-Ho Club.

No. I think... Wait a minute, now. Might have been! Because Hamp didn't get out of high school really until '46, I think. Sonny came out in '45. I think Hamp came out in '46. Might have been. I didn't play with that band, but I used to be in there all the time, you know.
